notes: Builtin provider registry. adapter/endpoint/protocol/allowedHosts/capabilities are authoritative; a LOCAL status overlay may only change enabled, priority, health, lastValidated and notes, and anything else it tries to change is refused and reported. Capability values were transcribed from docs/provider-protocols.md; 'null' means the service does not document a limit and no limit is enforced client side; 'verification.status' records how each provider was measured (live-tested, expected, or unverified). The overlay is read from disk and is NOT signed, so write access to it is a local trust decision. Re-probed live on 2026-09-11: see docs/evidence/live-probe-2026-09-11.md.

providers.label: ship.page
providers.protocolNotes: Documented reference is a JSON file map, but the live service accepts application/zip. The zip form is used because it preserves bytes exactly, which remote SHA-256 verification requires. UNVERIFIED in docs; live-tested.

cost.note: anonymous drops need no account; the documented lifetime differs by page, so the expiry is taken from the deploy response

claim.warning: The claim token is shown exactly once and grants ownership. Never forward it.

verification.note: live-tested: a 63-file artifact was served byte-identical for every file, HTML included. Re-measured 2026-09-11: a plain GET still receives byte-identical HTML, but a browser-like Accept header receives the upload plus a Cloudflare Insights beacon (+367 bytes on a 277-byte page), which verification now reports as browserRepresentation instead of hiding.

reachability.note: one mainland datacenter egress and one overseas egress; this is not a three-carrier or campus-network measurement

providers.label: ShipStatic
providers.protocolNotes: Live-verified: multipart/form-data with files[] (one part per file, filename carries the relative path) plus checksums (JSON array of MD5, same order) returns 201 {deployment,url,files,size,status,expires,claim}. Optional Idempotency-Key replays the original 201 for 24 h with Idempotency-Replay: true. Zero-byte file parts are dropped by the service parser and then rejected by the checksum count check.

claim.warning: Anyone holding the claim URL can take ownership of the deployment. Never forward it.

verification.note: live-tested: JS/CSS/font resources are served byte-identical. ShipStatic rewrites served HTML by appending a ?_ship=<id> cache-busting query to asset URLs, so HTML bytes differ and are not hash-verified. Its multipart parser also silently drops zero-byte file parts, so an artifact containing one is rejected as a capability failure before upload.

reachability.note: one mainland datacenter egress and one overseas egress; this is not a three-carrier or campus-network measurement

providers.label: aft.page
providers.protocolNotes: Live-verified: POST /api/v1/deploy with multipart parts file0, file0_path, file1, file1_path, ... returns {ok,slug,deployId,url,files,bytes,editToken,claimUrl,owned,notice}. The served HTML is NOT the uploaded HTML: aft.page injects a wrapper/summary page, so byte-exact verification fails.

ttl.source: 30 days idle; unclaimed sites are deleted after 30 days idle, so expiry is not a fixed deadline

claim.warning: The edit token and claim URL grant ownership. Never forward them.

verification.note: live-tested: aft.page does not serve the uploaded HTML at all - it injects a wrapper/summary page (a 416-byte index.html was served as 9873 bytes, 9461 without the import-map banner). Excluded from the default plan because its served output can never satisfy the verification contract.

reachability.note: one mainland datacenter egress and one overseas egress; this is not a three-carrier or campus-network measurement

providers.label: here.now
providers.protocolNotes: Live-verified 3-step flow: 1) POST /api/v1/publish with {files:[{path,size,contentType}]} and read upload.uploads[], upload.versionId, upload.finalizeUrl, siteUrl, publishStatus.expiresAt, claimToken, claimUrl. 2) PUT each file to the presigned *.r2.cloudflarestorage.com URL using exactly the returned headers. 3) POST upload.finalizeUrl with {versionId}; a null versionId is rejected with 400 invalid_type, so finalize is never called without one. Finalize is idempotent by versionId; concurrent finalize returns 409 finalize_in_flight with Retry-After.

claim.warning: The claim token is returned exactly once and grants ownership. Never forward it. The claimUrl must be copied byte for byte.

verification.note: live-tested: the create/finalize flow works (upload.versionId, upload.finalizeUrl, siteUrl) and JS/CSS/font resources are served byte-identical. An earlier 416-byte index.html was served as 798 bytes with injected Open Graph meta tags, so HTML bytes are not hash-verified; a 2026-09-11 re-probe served a minimal 86-byte page verbatim, so the rewriting is conditional — the presence-only policy stays conservative.

reachability.note: one mainland datacenter egress and one overseas egress; this is not a three-carrier or campus-network measurement

providers.label: EdgeOne Makers (anonymous)
providers.protocolNotes: edgeone makers deploy <dir> --anonymous; the anonymous preview is access-restricted and must be claimed within 60 minutes
providers.disabledReason: classification: login-free-upload-only. Anonymous deploy works with no account, but no reader can open the result: immediately after deploy the printed URL (and every variant, with or without the token, plain or browser-like headers) returned 401 "Access Restricted or Authentication Expired", whose page tells the visitor to obtain a link from the owner and the owner to mint one in the console; after the 60-minute claim window the same URLs return 404 because the unclaimed project is removed. Nothing was ever served. Evidence: research/edgeone-anonymous-measurement-2026-09-13.json

ttl.source: anonymous projects are removed unless claimed within 60 minutes

cost.note: public beta: anonymous deploys need no account

verification.note: classified 2026-09-13 as login-free-upload-only by a controlled matrix (two sites, 60 reads at 0/2/5/15/30/60s, query variants, two client profiles): never a 200, 401 while the project lived and 404 after the claim window closed. A second independent network was not available, so the cross-egress dimension is unmeasured.
